concerns.text: FR-001 (and US-1) require a minimum of **20 observations per species** ("filter for datasets with ... at least 20 observations per species"). FR-024 later mandates a **minimum of 30 observations per species** for the a priori power analysis. This creates a direct contradiction about the required sample size per species.
FR-024’s power‑analysis requirement (≥30 observations per species) conflicts with the earlier filtering rule (≥20 observations per species) without any stated reconciliation or conditional logic.

The description ‘nearest neighbor interpolation within a local radius (e.g., on the order of several kilometres)’ is vague; a concrete numeric radius (e.g., ≤5 km) is required to make the interpolation step measurable and testable.

FR‑021 mandates retrieval and storage of literature effect‑size values but does not specify where (file path, database) or in what format (JSON, CSV) they must be saved, nor how a verifier can confirm the retrieval succeeded.

SC‑006 requires coefficients to lie within literature‑reported effect‑size ±10 %, yet the spec provides no contingency for cases where the literature values cannot be obtained; without a defined fallback (e.g., use SC‑010), this criterion may be impossible to evaluate.

The edge‑case handling for missing ISRIC data mentions ‘nearest neighbor interpolation within a limited‑distance radius’ without defining the radius, making the behavior non‑deterministic and untestable.

FR-024 mandates an a‑priori power analysis targeting ≥80 % power and requires a minimum of 30 observations per species. The original idea only required ≥20 observations per species and did not call for a formal power analysis. This raises the data‑size requirement beyond what the research question explicitly demands.

FR-025 introduces a two‑stage missing‑nutrient policy (>30 % missing → exclusion, ≤30 % → species‑level mean imputation). The idea never specified any missing‑value handling beyond filtering for explicit P and N measurements, so this policy adds unrequested methodology.

FR-026 makes inclusion of additional environmental covariates (soil moisture, temperature, elevation) optional. The idea’s methodology did not mention these covariates; adding them changes the model specification and introduces potential omitted‑variable confounding that was not part of the original research question.

FR-021 requires retrieving peer‑reviewed literature values for expected nutrient effect sizes. The idea’s plan never called for external effect‑size retrieval; this step is extraneous to answering the stated question.

FR-011 mandates a sensitivity analysis against literature‑reported physiological ranges (±10 %). This analysis was not part of the original idea and is not required to test the hypothesised nutrient‑architecture relationship.
FR-028 adds a fallback sensitivity analysis (±15 % variation) when literature ranges are unavailable. This is an additional robustness check not requested in the idea.

FR-022 introduces a post‑report lint step scanning for causal language. The idea only warned against making causal claims in the discussion; a lint step was not specified and constitutes an unnecessary engineering addition.

The Linear Mixed‑Effects Model (FR‑004) includes species as a random intercept, yet the cross‑validation scheme (FR‑006) splits data strictly by species. When a species is held out, its random‑effect term cannot be estimated from the training data, making out‑of‑sample predictions for that species unreliable and rendering the reported out‑of‑sample adjusted R² (SC‑002) potentially invalid.

FR‑001 requires a minimum of 20 observations per species for inclusion, while the a priori power analysis (FR‑024) targets ≥30 observations per species to achieve 80 % power. Species with 20–29 observations will be retained but will not meet the power requirement, creating a mismatch that can leave the study under‑powered for many species and jeopardize the validity of SC‑009.

Success criterion SC‑002 defines achievement as the LMM adjusted R² being within 5 percentage points of the random‑forest R². Both metrics are derived from the same dataset and thus are not independent ground‑truth references for the hypothesised nutrient‑architecture relationship; using one model’s performance as a benchmark for the other creates a circular validation of the effect rather than an independent test of the hypothesis.

FR-026 makes inclusion of additional environmental covariates (soil moisture, temperature, elevation) optional. The idea’s methodology did not mention these covariates; adding them changes the model specification and introduces potential omitted‑variable confounding that was not part of the original research question.

new_concerns.text: FR-001 requires filtering for datasets with explicit phosphorus **and** nitrogen measurements (i.e., both nutrients must be present for all retained observations). FR-025, however, permits species to be retained when up to 30 % of observations lack a nutrient measurement and then imputes missing values using the species‑level mean. This creates a direct contradiction about whether missing nutrient values are allowed.

FR-003 mandates imputation of all missing values via k‑nearest‑neighbors (k=5) with a fallback to mean imputation. FR-025 specifies a different imputation strategy for nutrient‑missing values (species‑level mean). The two requirements conflict on the prescribed imputation method for the same missing‑data scenario.

FR-001 states the system MUST ensure at least **30 observations per species** after filtering. FR-032 introduces a contingency that, if power analysis fails, the system may relax the per‑species minimum to **20 observations**. This conditional relaxation contradicts the absolute requirement in FR-001.

SC-002 still defines success by comparing the LMM adjusted R² to the random‑forest R², which are both derived from the same dataset. This creates a circular validation because the benchmark (RF R²) is not an independent ground‑truth; the claim that the LMM performs adequately remains empirically unfalsifiable.

new_concerns.text: FR-004 specifies that species are included as a **fixed effect**, whereas the original idea required species to be treated as a **random effect** in the mixed‑effects model. This change alters the statistical framework and may affect the validity of the cross‑species inference, constituting a drift from the stated research methodology.
